function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t something that was “discovered” by a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been observed and studied for millennia. Here’s a quick overview of some key figures who helped uncover its nature:

| Person | Contribution |
|--------|--------------|
| **Thales of Miletus (c. 600 BCE)** | Noted that rubbing amber produced static electricity. |
| **William Gilbert (1544‑1603)** | Coined the term *electricus* and distinguished between magnetism and static electricity. |
| **Benjamin Franklin (1706‑1790)** | Demonstrated that lightning is electrical in nature (the kite experiment) and introduced the concept of positive/negative charge. |
| **Luigi Galvani (1737‑1798)** | Discovered bioelectricity—muscle contraction in frog legs when exposed to a spark. |
| **Alessandro Volta (1745‑1827)** | Invented the voltaic pile, the first chemical battery, providing a steady source of electric current. |
| **Hans Christian Ørsted (1777‑1851)** | Showed that electric currents produce magnetic fields, linking electricity and magnetism. |
| **Michael Faraday (1791‑1867)** | Developed electromagnetic induction, laying the groundwork for electric generators and motors. |
| **James Clerk Maxwell (1831‑1879)** | Unified electricity and magnetism into a single theory of electromagnetism. |

So while many scientists contributed to our understanding of electricity, it was a cumulative effort rather than a single discovery.
